risks.what: The 1999-2004 DXA files are six to eight times larger than the 2011-2018 ones while covering a similar number of participants.
risks.why: NCHS released the early whole-body DXA data with multiply imputed values for records that could not be measured, as several replicate rows per participant. If that is what the size difference is, a naive join on the participant identifier multiplies the cohort by the number of imputations and treats replicates of one person as independent observations -- which shrinks every standard error and makes a model look better than it is.
risks.beforeUse: Read the codebook for the early cycles and count rows per participant before joining anything. If replicates are present, either use a single imputation consistently or combine them by the published rules, and record which was done in the cohort flow. Do not average them into one row without saying so.
risks.note: This is inferred from file sizes alone and may be wrong. It is written down now because it is the kind of thing that is obvious in hindsight and invisible in a result.

risks.what: DXA eligibility ages are not the same across cycles.
risks.why: The preregistration fixes the population at 18-69. If a cycle stops at 59, that cycle contributes nothing above 59 and the age distribution of the training set is not what the cohort table suggests.
risks.beforeUse: Record the actual eligible age range per cycle from the codebooks and report the per-cycle age histogram in the cohort flow.
